 An early voting sign is seen Tuesday, March 31, 2026, at the community center at Creekmore Park in Fort Smith. Voters in the River Valley went to the polls Tuesday to participate in the primary and nonpartisan judicial election. Visit rivervalleydemocratgazette.com/rvphotos for today's photo gallery.
(River Valley Democrat-Gazette/Johnathan Brewer) 
 FORT SMITH -- Early voting for the city's mayoral runoff election between Christina Catsavis and Dan Williams begins at 8 a.m. Tuesday.
 Bonanza city residents will also decide who will represent them on the City Council. Alan Freeman and Maria Christenberry are vying for the Ward 1, Position 2 alderman's seat.
 Early voting in both races will take place in two Fort Smith locations: Room G8 of the Sebastian County Courthouse, 35 S. 6th St.; and the Ben Geren Park Tornado Shelter, 7700 Zero St.
 Polls will be open 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Tuesday through Nov. 30, but will be closed on Thursday, Nov. 26 (Thanksgiving), Saturday, Nov. 28, and Sunday, Nov. 29, according to the Sebastian County website.
 The election will be Dec. 1, and voters can also cast their ballots at one of 10 voting centers in Fort Smith and one in Bonanza from 7:30 a.m. to 7:30 p.m. that day.
 Catsavis and Williams were the top two vote-getters in a seven-way race in the Nov. 3 general election. They are in a runoff because no candidate garnered more than 50% of the vote.
 Catsavis finished with 7,091 votes to Williams' 5,273. The two received 61% of all votes cast in the mayor's race.
 Current Mayor George McGill announced earlier in the year he would not seek reelection.
 In Bonanza's Ward 1, Position 2 race, Christenberry led a field of three contenders with 78 votes to Freeman's 56 votes. Debra Collins received 50 votes, leaving Christenberry and Freeman to face each other in the runoff.
 -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- --
 Where to vote Dec. 1
 Voting centers open Dec. 1 in Fort Smith:
 Sebastian County Courthouse, 35 S. Sixth St.
 St. Luke Lutheran Church, 5401 Free Ferry Road
 Elm Grove Community Center/MLK Park, 1901 N. Greenwood Ave.
 Creekmore Park Recreation Building, 3301 S. M St.
 St. Bartholomew Episcopal, 2701 Old Greenwood Road
 Fort Smith Senior Activity Center, 2700 Cavanaugh Road
 East Side Baptist Church, 2710 Massard Road
 Connect Church, 3301 S. 66th St.
 Ben Geren Park Tornado Shelter, 7700 Zero St.
 In Bonanza:
 Bonanza Assembly of God, 701 McConnell St.
